title: Find Champion II
summary: In a tournament with n teams, represented by a directed acyclic graph (DAG), determine the unique champion if one exists.
statement: In a tournament with n teams, represented by a directed acyclic graph (DAG), determine the unique champion if one exists. A team is a champion if no other team is stronger. If there is no unique champion or the graph contains a cycle, return -1. Each team is numbered from 0 to n-1, and edges[i] = [ui, vi] denote a directed edge from team ui to team vi, indicating ui is stronger than vi.
constraints: Teams are numbered zero through n-1 and edges form a directed acyclic graph from stronger to weaker teams.
A champion has no incoming edge from any stronger team.
Return the unique champion, or -1 when more than one team has indegree zero.
reference_solution:
def find_unique_champion(n,edges):
    indegree=[0]*n
    for _,weaker in edges:indegree[weaker]+=1
    candidates=[team for team,value in enumerate(indegree) if value==0]
    return candidates[0] if len(candidates)==1 else -1

hints: Every edge proves its destination has a stronger team.
Count incoming edges and collect teams with indegree zero.
Return the sole zero-indegree team; otherwise return -1.
In a DAG every champion candidate is exactly a source, and uniqueness is the only remaining requirement.

tests.explanation: Only team zero has no incoming edge, so it is the champion.
Teams zero and one both have no incoming edge, so no unique champion exists.
